# Day-to-day alignment study (supplementary, post-test; generated by scripts/analyze_alignment_study.py)

What was done: 81 EEGNet models (full-22, relevance-16, relevance-8; 9 participants; seeds 0, 1, 2) were trained with the frozen recipe on session 1 after Euclidean alignment. Alignment multiplies each recording day by the inverse square root of that day's average spatial covariance, so that on average the electrodes vary together in the same way on both days. It needs no labels. The aligned models were scored on session 2 three ways:

- ea-all: session 2 aligned with all of its trials. Offline only: it needs the whole day in advance.
- ea-first-run: session 2 aligned with its first run (48 trials) and scored on runs 2-6. An online system could do this after a short warm-up.
- none: the aligned model fed session-2 trials that were not aligned; shows how much it relies on alignment.

Every number is paired with the archived unaligned model of the same participant, seed and electrodes, scored on the same trials.

## What this can and cannot show

- Alignment uses session-2 trials without their labels: all of them for ea-all, only the first run for ea-first-run. The frozen protocol uses no session-2 data before scoring, so this is outside it.
- Exploratory: planned after the main study's test results were known. It does not replace the frozen final configuration (relevance-16-prune50, INT8).
- Nine participants. An interval that contains zero does not show that alignment changes nothing, and none of this shows how new people would fare.

## How to read the numbers

Accuracy is the share of artifact-free session-2 trials classified correctly (four classes, chance 25%), averaged over seeds within each participant; tables give the mean of the nine participants. Differences are in percentage points (pp), written as mean [95% interval] better/worse: the interval resamples the nine participants (10,000 bootstrap resamples, seed 690), and better/worse counts participants whose accuracy is higher/lower (the rest are tied).

| relevance-8 minus full-22 | artifact-free trials of runs 2-6 (ea-first-run) | -5.62 [-9.32, -1.51] 2/7 | -4.60 [-9.62, +0.32] 3/6 | +1.02 [-3.31, +5.37] 5/4 |

## Participant 2

Participant 2's day-2 signals are about 1.5 times larger than on day 1 (measured in the electrode-count study), the clearest case of the shift that alignment is meant to remove.

- full-22: all trials 38.9% unaligned, 50.1% aligned (+11.2 pp, rank 1 of 9); runs 2-6 37.1% unaligned, 47.1% aligned with run 1 (+10.0 pp). Mean gain from ea-all without participant 2: -0.05 pp, against +1.20 pp with all nine.
- relevance-16: all trials 47.6% unaligned, 49.1% aligned (+1.5 pp, rank 6 of 9); runs 2-6 46.6% unaligned, 47.5% aligned with run 1 (+1.0 pp). Mean gain from ea-all without participant 2: +2.65 pp, against +2.53 pp with all nine.
- relevance-8: all trials 42.3% unaligned, 43.0% aligned (+0.7 pp, rank 5 of 9); runs 2-6 41.1% unaligned, 41.6% aligned with run 1 (+0.6 pp). Mean gain from ea-all without participant 2: +2.20 pp, against +2.03 pp with all nine.
- relevance-16 minus full-22, unaligned (archived models), all trials: participant 2 +8.7 pp (nine-participant mean +1.17 pp).
- relevance-16 minus full-22, aligned (ea-all), all trials: participant 2 -0.9 pp (nine-participant mean +2.49 pp).
- relevance-8 minus full-22, unaligned (archived models), all trials: participant 2 +3.4 pp (nine-participant mean -5.12 pp).
- relevance-8 minus full-22, aligned (ea-all), all trials: participant 2 -7.1 pp (nine-participant mean -4.29 pp).
